title: reduce streaming token latency: token loop, adaptive flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, KV cache and batching
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming token latency has been a persistent issue for low-latency applications. High tail latency was traced to a combination of token-loop flushing cadence, synchronous backpressure propagation, suboptimal kernel scheduling, and missed KV-cache warm paths under continuous batching. This PR implements a coordinated set of runtime changes to reduce p50/p95 token emission latency while preserving throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Refactor token emission loop to an event-driven async loop with non-blocking flush triggers; 2) Add adaptive flush cadence: flush cadence adapts to active batch sizes and model step-time percentiles to avoid unnecessary small flushes; 3) Introduce soft backpressure gating that propagates best-effort early signals to the batcher without stalling fast flows; 4) Improve kernel scheduling priority for streaming requests by adding a short-lived high-priority queue for first-token generation work and small-seq attention kernels; 5) KV-cache warm-path optimization: prefetch and pin commonly-accessed KV pages during continuous batching, and avoid evicting pinned pages on short-lived slots; 6) Continuous-batching heuristic tweaks: lower minimum batch hold time for small interactive streams and dynamic batch size thresholds based on observed inter-arrival times; 7) Observability: new metrics (streaming.flush_latency_ms, streaming.backpressure_events, kernel.priority_queue_wait_ms, kvcache.hits_pinned) and dashboards; 8) Feature flag and runtime knobging for gradual rollout. Implementation notes: The token loop change pulled the per-request state machine into a lightweight async runner to minimize context switches. Adaptive flush cadence uses EWMA of per-step latencies with configurable min/max cadence and a small hysteresis window. Backpressure gating sends a one-way hint to the batcher which may prefer draining larger work but will not block already-scheduled fast paths. Kernel scheduling change is implemented in scheduler.cpp: add PrioritySlot and a short-term priority window to favor low-latency kernels; scheduling fallbacks ensure no starvation. KV cache change implements a pinned set and a best-effort prefetch on new streaming sessions. Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added for token loop and KV-cache semantics. Performance harness run across small (gpt-medium), medium (gpt-large), and LLM-1B variants; microbenchmarks run on both A100 and T4 nodes. Canary rollout: 5% of streaming traffic for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours before full rollout. Results summary included below. Backwards compatibility: All changes behind feature flag "streaming-low-latency"; default behavior unchanged until rollout. Checklist: [x] Backend unit tests [x] Integration tests with streaming clients [x] Performance benchmarks and regression tests [x] Canaried rollout plan [x] Docs/observability updated Related: references ENG-9123, ENG-9199 and incident SUP-442.

performance_summary: End-to-end streaming token emission latency improvements observed in controlled benchmarks: p50 per-token emission latency reduced from ~42ms to ~18ms (57% improvement) on 2k-step sessions, p95 reduced from ~120ms to ~55ms (54% improvement) for interactive traces. First-token latency on small sequences improved by ~35% due to kernel priority slot. Overall throughput remained within 3% of baseline for large-batch workloads. KV-cache pinned pages increased hit-rate from 76% to 91% on continuous-batching traces. CPU-side scheduling overhead decreased ~9% as measured by scheduler.priority_queue_wait_ms. Canary metrics showed no increase in OOM events and error rates remained stable.

release_notes: Runtime: improve streaming token emission latency via adaptive flush cadence, soft backpressure gating, kernel scheduling priority for low-latency kernels, and KV-cache prefetch/pinning. Default behavior behind feature flag 'streaming-low-latency'.
notes: This is a coordinated runtime change touching the scheduler, batcher, token loop and KV-cache; keep rollout conservative and monitor streaming.flush_latency_ms and kvcache.hits_pinned closely during first 48h.
